title: Image input: detail levels, token cost and limits
summary: Images are billed as input tokens. The `detail` setting and the model family decide how the image is resized and counted, so the same photo can cost 85 or 10,000 tokens.
useIf: You send photos, scans or screenshots to a vision model and must predict cost, TPM load and accuracy.
avoidIf: A text extraction service already returns what you need, which is cheaper than any image token.

explain.md: Vision models turn an image into input tokens, and those tokens count toward your TPM limit [[r1]]. Two schemes exist. **Patch models** cover the image with 32 px patches and multiply by a model factor. **Tile models** charge base tokens plus tokens per 512 px tile. `detail` accepts `low`, `high`, `original` or `auto` and defaults to `auto`, whose meaning differs by family (checked 2026-10-13).

explain.title: Patch model cost
explain.expr: tokens = ceil( min(patches, budget) x multiplier ), patches = ceil(w/32) x ceil(h/32)

vars.v: 1.2 for gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.2; 1.62 for the gpt-4.1-mini 2025-04-14 snapshot
2,500 patches at `high`; 10,000 at `original` on gpt-5.5; images over 30,000 patches are rejected

explain.example: gpt-5.5 at `high`, 1536 x 1024: 48 x 32 = 1,536 patches, so **1,844** tokens. A 2048 x 2048 image shrinks to 2,500 patches and costs **3,000**.

explain.title: Tile model cost
explain.expr: tokens = base + tiles x tile_tokens, and `low` = base only

vars.v: gpt-4o and gpt-4.1: 85 and 170. gpt-4o-mini: 2,833 and 5,667. gpt-5.1: 70 and 140

explain.example: gpt-4.1, 1024 x 1024 at `high`: scaled to 768, 4 tiles, 85 + 4 x 170 = **765** tokens (derived from the rules, not printed in the docs).

explain.md: Limits: OpenAI lists 512 MB per request, 1,500 images per request and 30,000 patches per image, and it rejects larger images instead of shrinking them [[r1]]. Azure's vision chat page lists 20 MB per image and 10 images per call [[r17]]. Use the stricter number for Azure-hosted deployments and test on the exact deployment. Image tokens and the rest of the prompt must also fit the model's input and context limits, so a token estimate alone does not guarantee a request passes [[r1]].

explain.title: `low` is not always cheaper
explain.md: On the gpt-5.4 family `low` gets a 6,144-patch budget, so it can cost more than `high`. Compute with the model's own formula or the OpenAI image cost calculator before budgeting.

whereToUse: Intake of photos, screenshots and scans where a vision model reads or classifies them
Computer-use and UI agents that need clicks to land on exact pixels
Batch pipelines with a token budget and a TPM ceiling
Model migrations where the image bill can change without a code change

use: `low` for coarse scenes or classification on a tile model
`high` as the pinned default when you can accept resizing
`original` for dense pages, small print, small objects and computer use, where the model supports it
avoid: Leaving `detail` on `auto` in production: it maps to different behaviour per family
Sending huge scans unshrunk: over 30,000 patches the request fails
Estimating cost from file size: tokens depend on pixel dimensions and the model, not bytes
flips: Moving from a tile model to a patch model: re-estimate cost, since the formulas differ
Coordinates matter: use `original`, resize yourself and map coordinates back
TPM becomes the bottleneck: lower resolution before lowering model quality

pitfalls.symptom: The image bill changes after a model swap
pitfalls.cause: Patch and tile models count differently, and `auto` maps differently
pitfalls.fix: Pin `detail`, compute with the target model's rule, and log image tokens per request.

pitfalls.cause: The image was resized, so returned coordinates no longer match screen pixels
pitfalls.fix: Resize to a known size yourself and map coordinates back.

pitfalls.symptom: A big scan returns an error
pitfalls.cause: The image exceeds 30,000 patches after processing and is rejected, not shrunk

scenarios.title: Nightly scans with small print
scenarios.situation: A batch reads 200,000 A4 scans at 300 dpi (2480 x 3508 px) every night on a patch model of the gpt-5.5 type. TPM and the nightly window are both tight, and some pages have small print.
unknowns: Can failing pages be identified in advance?
scenarios.question: Which `detail` do you ship?

options.name: Pin `high`, measure on a labelled sample, move only failing page types to `original`
options.why: `high` is at most 3,000 tokens a page. `original` is 78 x 110 = 8,580 patches, so 10,296 tokens (derived), about 3.4 times more.
options.tradeoff: You build a labelled sample and a routing rule.

options.name: `original` for every page
options.why: Best reading accuracy with no routing logic.
options.tradeoff: Over 2 billion tokens a night against under 0.6 billion at `high`, which can exhaust TPM.

options.name: Leave `detail` unset
options.why: On this family `auto` equals `original`, so cost jumps silently and changes again if you swap models.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable in a prototype on one pinned model.

flips.if: Only digits in a fixed region matter
flips.then: Crop that region and send it, or use a layout service and skip the image tokens.

flips.if: Volume drops to a few hundred pages
flips.then: Use `original` everywhere and stop engineering routing.

scenarios.takeaway: Pin detail, price it with the model's formula, and escalate per page type.

scenarios.title: Product thumbnails at scale
scenarios.situation: A catalogue service tags millions of 1024 x 1024 product photos with a coarse category. Latency matters and the team is choosing between a tile model and a gpt-5.4 family model.
unknowns: Are fine details such as logos needed?
Is the model fixed by policy?
scenarios.question: How do you set `detail` and pick the family?

options.name: `low` on a tile model such as gpt-4.1
options.why: `low` costs only the base tokens, 85 for gpt-4.1, whatever the image size, against 765 at `high`.

options.name: `high` on a tile model
options.why: Keeps more detail for the same category task.
options.tradeoff: Nine times the tokens of `low` for a coarse label.

options.name: `low` on a gpt-5.4 family model, assuming it is cheapest
options.why: `low` there has a 6,144-patch budget and can cost more than `high`.
options.tradeoff: Fine only after you compute the real count and find it acceptable.

flips.then: Downscale images yourself so the patch count stays small.

scenarios.takeaway: A cheap label belongs on a flat-cost `low`, and `low` is not cheap everywhere.

quiz.q: A patch model with multiplier 1.2 and a 2,500 patch budget at `detail: high` receives a 1536 x 1024 image. How many billable image tokens?
quiz.explain: 48 x 32 = 1,536 patches, under the 2,500 budget and within 2048 px. 1,536 x 1.2 = 1,843.2, rounded up to 1,844.

quiz.q: After a model swap, `detail: low` image tokens rise per request. Which cause fits best?
options: The gpt-5.4 family gives `low` a 2048 px and 6,144-patch budget, so it can exceed `high`
The API retried the request and billed twice
quiz.explain: On the gpt-5.4 family `low` is not a flat small image. Tile models charge only base tokens at `low`. The multiplier is not applied that way, and retries are unrelated.

quiz.q: Put the patch-model token estimate in order.
items: Fit the image to the detail level's pixel limit
Shrink if over the patch budget and recount
Multiply by the model multiplier and round up
quiz.explain: Resize first, count patches, apply the budget, then multiply. Over 30,000 patches the request is rejected before any multiplier.

flashcards.front: What is the patch-model image token formula?
flashcards.back: ceil(w/32) x ceil(h/32) patches, shrunk to the budget if needed, times the model multiplier (1.2 for current GPT-5.x), rounded up.

flashcards.front: What does `detail: low` cost on a tile model?
flashcards.back: Only the base tokens, regardless of image size: 85 for gpt-4o and gpt-4.1, 70 for gpt-5.1.
`auto` maps to different behaviour per family: `original` on gpt-5.5 and gpt-6-astra, `high` on gpt-5.4. A model swap silently changes cost.
